title: A.e. on an open set, a function agreeing with a coordinate of a Lipschitz map has the projected Fréchet derivative
statement: Let k, Q ∈ ℕ, let Ω ⊆ ℝ^k (ℝ^k = Eucl k) be open, C ≥ 0 (C : ℝ≥0), v : ℝ^k → ℝ^Q C-Lipschitz on Ω (LipschitzOnWith C v Ω), c ∈ Fin Q, and g : ℝ^k → ℝ any function with g(w) = EuclideanSpace.proj c (v(w)) for every w ∈ Ω. Then for Lebesgue-almost every w ∈ ℝ^k: if w ∈ Ω, then fderiv ℝ g w x = EuclideanSpace.proj c (fderiv ℝ v w x) for every x ∈ ℝ^k. Here fderiv is Mathlib's Fréchet derivative, defined as 0 at points of non-differentiability; no regularity of g is assumed.
lean_statement: ∀ (k Q : ℕ) (Ω : Set (Eucl k)) (C : ℝ≥0) (v : Eucl k → Eucl Q) (c : Fin Q) (g : Eucl k → ℝ), IsOpen Ω → LipschitzOnWith C v Ω → EqOn g (fun w => EuclideanSpace.proj c (v w)) Ω → ∀ᵐ w ∂(volume : Measure (Eucl k)), w ∈ Ω → ∀ x : Eucl k, fderiv ℝ g w x = EuclideanSpace.proj c (fderiv ℝ v w x)
